parsed.attack: Name the recipient of the shared teardown log and the loop dies on the spot: the forum reader who admires a pinned-bolt record cannot install anything, because using it requires a Ray-Ban Display and a Neural Band, roughly $800 of hardware, so the conversion step is not 'download a $30 app' but 'buy a headset for a hobby notebook'. The artifact is also only produced when a restoration finishes, a six-to-eighteen-month cycle, so even a generous coefficient compounds once a year - against the rule that a 3-day loop beats a stronger 30-day one, this is a 365-day loop. The reachable population, home-garage motorcycle restorers who already own a Display, is plausibly in the hundreds worldwide, which is below the founder's own 500-unit kill line before the loop runs at all.
parsed.strongest_defence: Early-adopter overlap is the whole bet: people who bought $800 glasses are precisely the gadget-forward hobbyists who post long build threads, and because the population is tiny it can be saturated by hand - one sustained ADVrider or Britbike thread plus a few YouTube restorers could reach every Display-owning restorer alive without spending anything.
parsed.verdict_reason: The share reaches people who cannot install without $800 of hardware, and the hardware-gated audience is smaller than the first thousand users the loop would need to produce, with no unpaid path to more.
